newsitem.title: USA: N. Hampshire House passes Gov's kindergarten plan.
newsitem.headline: N. Hampshire House passes Gov's kindergarten plan.

text.p: New Hampshire Gov. Jeanne Shaheen Thursday defeated a plan by Republican rival House Speaker Donna Sytek to gut her $50 million statewide kindergarten plan.

After more than two hours of debate, the Democrat governor's plan to spend $1,000 per student and provide communities with 100 percent grants totalling $30 million to build kindergarten classrooms passed in a dramatic 247 to 135 vote.
Shaheen had campaigned for the kindergarten issue, but Republicans in the Legislature were determined to either kill or pare down the proposal.
House Speaker Sytek and the House Finance Committee had recommended passage of a plan spending millions of dollars less than Shaheen's plan.
Sytek said the governor's plan was too expensive and was unfair to communities faced with other public education spending priorities. But Sytek's plan went down to defeat in a 189 to 184 vote.
Shaheen had enlisted a bi-partisan group of lawmakers headed by former GOP Majority Leader Ann Torr of Dover to pass her plan. The governor's bill now moves to the state Senate.
